ai.description: *Rohanixalus vittatus* (Rhacophoridae) is a small treefrog (20–30 mm) with a pale brown back and distinct dark brown lateral stripes. It features translucent skin and prominent, expanded toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rohanixalus vittatus* is best distinguished by the distinct, continuous dark brown lateral stripe running from the snout tip through the eye to the groin.
ai.habitat: *Rohanixalus vittatus* inhabits tropical evergreen and deciduous forests, often found in bushes and shrubs near water bodies at elevations up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Rohanixalus vittatus is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among vegetation near temporary pools and water bodies.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rohanixalus vittatus* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 20–60 eggs in foam nests attached to leaves overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Rohanixalus vittatus* is found in Northeast India, primarily across Assam, Meghalaya, and Manipur, inhabiting low-to-mid elevation forests and wetlands.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Rohanixalus vittatus* consists of a series of short, high-pitched "tink" or "click" notes, typically heard in rice paddies and marshy habitats.
